title: Lax monoidal functors into cartesian targets as product-cone functors
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Use the cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $r:\mathcal C^{\otimes}\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be a symmetric monoidal infinity category: a cocartesian fibration whose fiber over $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ is $\mathcal C^n$ via the inert projections $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$; inert means every non-basepoint of the target has exactly one preimage. Let $\mathcal D$ be an infinity category with finite products and let $\mathcal D^{\times}$ be its cartesian symmetric monoidal infinity category of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. A lax symmetric monoidal functor to $\mathcal D^{\times}$ means a functor $H:\mathcal C^{\otimes}\to\mathcal D^{\times}$ over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ preserving cocartesian arrows over inert maps. Such functors are equivalently functors $F:\mathcal C^{\otimes}\to\mathcal D$ for which, for every tuple $c=(c_i)_{i=1}^n$, the arrows $F(c)\to F(c_i)$ induced by the inert cocartesian projections exhibit $F(c)$ as $\prod_iF(c_i)$, including $F(())$ terminal for $n=0$. In this correspondence $H$ has underlying functor $F|_{\mathcal C}$, and its $n$-ary comparison is
$$\prod_iF(c_i)\simeq F((c_i))\xrightarrow{F(\mu)}F\left(\bigotimes_i c_i\right),$$
where $\mu$ is a cocartesian lift in $\mathcal C^{\otimes}$ of the fold map $\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$. The correspondence includes natural transformations and all higher homotopies. For a fixed $F$ with its product-cone property, the space of lifts $H$ equipped with this identification is contractible.

source.place: Definition 2.4.1.1 (lax Cartesian structures) and Proposition 2.4.1.7; Ramzi 2209.12569v2, proof of Theorem 2.1, first displayed equivalence. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Let $\Gamma^{\times}$ be the ordinary category of pairs $(\langle n\rangle,S)$ and arrows over $\alpha$ with $\alpha^{-1}(T)\subseteq S$, and let $v:N(\Gamma^{\times})\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be its cartesian fibration. Form the relative exponential $q:Q\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ whose simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ are maps $\Delta^k\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\Gamma^{\times})\to\mathcal D$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential], $Q$ is a quasicategory, $q$ is cocartesian, and its fiber over $\langle n\rangle$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(N(B_n),\mathcal D)$, with the stated cocartesian-edge criterion. Let $P\subset Q$ be the full product-diagram subcategory. The recognition statement [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition] identifies $P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ over the base with the cartesian symmetric monoidal infinity category $\mathcal D^{\times}$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope], including its inert cocartesian arrows, mapping spaces, composition, and all higher simplices. Thus we may work with the relative-exponential model $P$ while retaining the canonical target.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, together with HTT Corollary 3.2.2.13; the product-diagram recognition is the explicit identification of the full subcategory with the cartesian envelope.

proof.text: Put $X=\mathcal C^{\otimes}\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\Gamma^{\times})$. The relative-exponential universal property in [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] gives, naturally in every simplicial parameter, $$\operatorname{Hom}_{/N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}(K,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(K\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\Gamma^{\times}),\mathcal D).$$ Consequently a functor $H:\mathcal C^{\otimes}\to P\subset Q$ over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ is exactly a coherent diagram $G:X\to\mathcal D$ whose restriction $S\mapsto G(c,S)$ lies in the product-diagram subcategory $P_n$ for every tuple $c$; the equivalence is on simplices, so it retains all higher homotopies. The full-subset section $A\subset X$ is canonically $\mathcal C^{\otimes}$, since every pointed map has inverse image of the full target subset contained in the full source subset. Evaluation on this section is therefore $F=G|_A$, the underlying functor used in the classification.

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Remark 2.4.1.3, Construction 2.4.1.4, and proof of Proposition 2.4.1.7, identification of the relative-exponential diagram categories.

proof.text: Fix $x=(c,S)\in X$. Choose an $r$-cocartesian edge $u_S:c\to c_S$ over the inert selector $\sigma_S:\langle n\rangle\to S_*$, which keeps precisely the elements of $S$; $S_*$ may be identified with the corresponding standard pointed set. It defines $\widetilde u_S:(c,S)\to(c_S,S)$ with target in $A$. This is initial in $A_{x/}$. In fact, an object of that comma category is an arrow $x\to(d,\{1,\ldots,m\})$ over some $\alpha$ with $\alpha^{-1}\{1,\ldots,m\}\subseteq S$. There is exactly one pointed map $\beta:S_*\to\langle m\rangle$ with $\alpha=\beta\sigma_S$. The cocartesian mapping-space criterion in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] says that the space of factorizations of the given edge through $u_S$, over this $\beta$ and with its specified comparison homotopy, is contractible. This is exactly the mapping space from $\widetilde u_S$ to that comma object. This proof works for $S=\varnothing$ and for the full subset, where the selector is the identity.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.1.7, initial object of the comma category C_(C,S)/; explicit cocartesian mapping-space verification.

proof.text: Let $F:A\to\mathcal D$ be any functor. The opposite-category application of [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] to the initial object just found shows that its diagram on $A_{x/}$ has a limit $F(c_S)$. Apply the right-hand dual in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence] to $A\subseteq X$ and $\mathcal D\to *$. The latter is an isofibration because $\mathcal D$ is a quasicategory and the identity equivalence of the point lifts to an identity at every object. The local limits therefore give a coherent right Kan extension $G:X\to\mathcal D$ with $G|_A=F$, and the cone comparison $G(c,S)\to F(c_S)$ is an equivalence. These local limits also show that an extension is a right Kan extension precisely when it takes every $\widetilde u_S$ to an equivalence: a cone on a category with an initial object is limiting exactly when its component at that initial object is an equivalence. To check this last criterion, compare to the limit at the initial value furnished by the cited final-index lemma and use the defining uniqueness of a limiting cone. Finally [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] makes restriction fully faithful on right Kan extensions, since the target of any pair has the required limiting cones. Thus extensions exist and their coherent transformations are determined by restriction; no completeness of $\mathcal D$ beyond the local limits is invoked.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.1.7, right Kan extension and HTT 4.3.2.15; here expanded through the existing Kan existence and mapping-restriction nodes.

proof.text: Suppose $F$ has the product-cone property in the statement and $G$ is its right Kan extension. Step 4 gives $G(c,S)\simeq F(c_S)$ and $G(c,\{i\})\simeq F(c_i)$. Applying the product-cone hypothesis to the tuple $c_S$ therefore shows that every $G(c,S)\to\prod_{i\in S}G(c,\{i\})$ is an equivalence, with the actual restriction cone maps. Hence $G$ defines $H$ by step 2. For an inert cocartesian edge $v:c\to d$ over $\alpha$ and any subset $T$ of the output coordinates, the composite selector to $d_T$ is cocartesian and selects exactly $\alpha^{-1}T$ in $c$. The composite is cocartesian because a composite of cocartesian edges is cocartesian [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] (equivalently, by pasting the homotopy-pullback squares of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]). Since $\alpha$ is inert it restricts to a bijection $\alpha^{-1}T\to T$, and $\sigma_T\alpha$ is $\sigma_{\alpha^{-1}T}$ followed by the induced isomorphism $(\alpha^{-1}T)_*\cong T_*$. Composing the selector from $c$ to $c_{\alpha^{-1}T}$ with a cocartesian lift of this isomorphism (an equivalence) gives another cocartesian lift of $\sigma_T\alpha$; cocartesian lifts are initial in the lift category of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], so the two are identified by an equivalence over the identity, and the composite selector is the selector of $\alpha^{-1}T$ up to this relabelling. Right Kan extension sends both selector arrows to equivalences, so two-out-of-three makes $G(c,\alpha^{-1}T)\to G(d,T)$ an equivalence. For singletons these are exactly the component equivalences characterizing an inert cocartesian arrow of the target [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Thus $H$ is lax symmetric monoidal.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.1.7, implication (1′),(2′) to (1),(2), including empty subsets.

proof.text: Conversely let $H$ be lax symmetric monoidal and let $G$ be its subset diagram. The fiberwise product condition holds by construction of the model in step 1. Its preservation of inert cocartesian arrows makes $G(c,S)\to G(c_S,S)$ an equivalence for every selector, using the component-equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. The case of a subset with several elements follows from the singleton cases by the product-cone comparisons, and the empty case is the unique map between terminal objects. Step 4 therefore says that $G$ is the right Kan extension of $F=G|_A$. Moreover $G(c,\{1,\ldots,n\})\simeq\prod_iG(c,\{i\})\simeq\prod_iG(c_i,\{i\})$, and the maps are the images under $F$ of the inert projections. This is exactly the desired product-cone condition on $F$, including the empty product. Steps 5 and 6 identify the lax functor diagrams with the right Kan extensions of precisely those $F$. Their equivalence on all transformations and higher homotopies follows from the mapping-space restriction equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction], rather than from an objectwise coherence assertion.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.1.7, implication (1),(2) to (1′),(2′), and equivalence on full functor categories.

proof.text: Evaluation at $\langle1\rangle$ is evaluation of the subset diagram at its sole nonempty subset, so the underlying functor of $H$ is $F|_{\mathcal C}$. For a cocartesian lift $\mu:c\to\bigotimes_i c_i$ of the fold map, its target's only nonempty subset has inverse image the full source subset. The block map of $H(\mu)$ is therefore exactly $F(c)\to F(\bigotimes_i c_i)$. Identifying $F(c)$ with $\prod_iF(c_i)$ by its given cone gives the displayed comparison, in the required direction. With no inputs its source is $G(c,\varnothing)=F(())$, terminal; this supplies the nullary comparison. These identifications are identities of evaluation and restriction in the subset-diagram model, so they retain the functor's entire coherent simplex data.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.7, evaluation on the full-subset section; Ramzi 2209.12569v2 Theorem 2.1, and Remark 2.2 for the operation formula.

proof.text: Fix a product-cone functor $F$ and include its specified identification in the lifting data. Existence is step 4 followed by step 5. For any two such lifted diagrams, [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] identifies their full transformation mapping space with that of their restrictions. Taking the homotopy fiber over the specified identity of $F$ therefore gives a contractible space. Its points are equivalences: lifting the inverse identity gives an inverse, and lifting the two identity composites gives the inverse homotopies. The same mapping-space fibers retain all their higher homotopies. Thus the nonempty space of lifts with identification has contractible paths and higher path spaces, and is contractible. This proves the final uniqueness assertion without importing Proposition 2.4.1.7 itself as an uncited black box.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.1.7, contractible right Kan extension choices (equivalence consequence of the trivial Kan fibration).
